newsitem.title: USA: U.S. leaves door open to troops staying in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. leaves door open to troops staying in Bosnia.

text.p: A senior U.S. State Department official on Thursday left open the possibility that U.S. troops could remain in Bosnia past June 1998 when Defense Secretary William Cohen insists they will be gone.

The official, briefing reporters on the adminstration's new initiative to intensify Bosnia peace efforts, was asked if U.S. troops would be out of Bosnia in June 1998. He replied: "I'm not making any commitment. The president has not yet made any commitment."

The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, briefed reporters on a six-week review by the administration on Bosnia policy. He said it did not address the future of NATO-led peacekeeping forces, but dealt with civilian aspects of the U.S.-brokered Bosnian peace accord of 1995.
The mandate for the current NATO-led force, known as SFOR, is due to expire in June 1998.

Asked if SFOR might emerge afterwards in another form, the official said: "That is an issue that the president will be addressing at a future time, I'm sure. What has been decided is a statement of fact: The SFOR mandate ends in June 1998 and the future still has to be decided."

He briefed reporters ahead of a speech by secretary of State Madeleine Albright in which the United States pledges to intensify efforts to ensure a stable peace in Bosnia and to use all levers at its disposal to make that happen.
